clue.text: Never missing out on any social function whatever happens

definitions.text: Never missing out on any social function
definitions.meaning: read literally, someone who turns up at every party or gathering is present at each one
the everyday idiom meaning in any case, regardless of circumstances

explanation.surface: A dedicated socialite refuses to miss a single party, come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for regardless, and taken word by word it describes perfect attendance at functions.

clue.text: To call for silence is nonsense

parts.note: SH is the hushing sound used to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone declares that demanding quiet is foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym for rubbish or twaddle.

clue.text: Tool turned to acquisition of ill-gotten gains

indicators.note: the word tool is turned round, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A tool becomes a burglar's instrument for acquiring stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plunder or stolen booty.

clue.text: Levelling off at the end of the day

definitions.meaning: the time after afternoon, before night

explanation.surface: Something flattens out as day draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Present participle of making level, and also the time of day around dusk.

clue.text: Sound come-back if House supports the Euro idea

indicators.note: in a down clue the house goes underneath, holding up the European piece

parts.note: EC is the European Community, the European project

explanation.surface: A politician returns, backing the European ideal if parliament supports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' works because this is a down entry: the house sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound that returns to the hearer is a returning noise.

clue.text: A tower on agricultural land

parts.note: read 'tower' as one who tows, not a tall building: the farm vehicle that pulls ploughs and trailers

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a tall building standing in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The farm vehicle tows ploughs and trailers, so it is literally a tow-er.

clue.text: Military drop-out

parts.note: not a deserter but a soldier who literally drops out of an aircraft

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a soldier who has quit the army.
explanation.definitionFit: An airborne soldier jumps from a plane, literally dropping out of it.

clue.text: Undertaking final tax demand

definitions.meaning: read as the tasks of an undertaker, the funeral director's work
inheritance tax levied on an estate after someone dies

explanation.surface: A business venture receives its last bill from the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: The tax on a dead person's estate, punned as a funeral director's jobs.

clue.text: Arrived from the East by river

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone describes reaching a place by travelling from the east along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' looks like a direction of travel or a reversal signal, but it simply supplies E, placed after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple past-tense synonym: to have reached a place is to have got there.

clue.text: Ram thoughtfully?

parts.note: a male sheep butts with its skull, so it literally employs that body part; the idiom means to think sensibly

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction to charge at something in a considered way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means think things through, and a butting sheep does it literally with its skull.

clue.text: The lure of sex appeal to some degree

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree
IT is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 1920s film star the It Girl

explanation.surface: A remark that attraction works partly through sexual charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lure is something used to entice, as on a fishing hook.

clue.text: All out for a lot of bacon

definitions.meaning: with full commitment, holding nothing back

explanation.surface: Someone goes to any lengths to get a lot of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing something completely, read literally as an entire pig.

clue.text: He'd hated war breaking out in the Tory Party

indicators.note: the letters break apart and re-form in a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving three letters

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is said to have loathed the outbreak of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' signals the anagram of HEDHATEDWAR. He was Conservative Prime Minister of the UK from 1970 to 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the British Conservative Party and was Prime Minister in the early 1970s.

clue.text: Monstrous serpent reaches Northern Territory water source

parts.note: the Hydra was the many-headed serpent monster slain by Hercules
NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: A giant snake arrives in outback Australia looking for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A street fire-plug that firefighters tap is a supply point for water.

clue.text: Poison the bully beef?

parts.note: bully beef is corned beef sold canned, so picture the bovine animal sealed inside a can

explanation.surface: A sinister plan to contaminate the tinned corned beef.
explanation.walkthrough: Bully beef is tinned corned beef, a British army ration; OX inside TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisonous substance, here pictured as cattle meat sealed in a can.

clue.text: Put one's finger on reason for irrational behaviour?

definitions.meaning: made physical contact with, pressed lightly with a fingertip
slightly mad, as in informal 'a bit ...', which would explain odd conduct

explanation.surface: Someone tries to pin down why a person is acting so strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: past tense of contacting with the hand, and informal for mildly unhinged.

clue.text: Times needs a casual office assistant first

indicators.note: says the office worker goes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single thing

explanation.surface: A newspaper needs an office temp to start the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is plural: musical speeds, the plural of tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical speeds; the Italian plural of tempo, the pace of a piece.

clue.text: George the First as a cipher, or very soon to be one!

parts.note: G is the initial of George
the regnal numeral I, written out as a word
a royal cipher ends in R for Rex, king, as in the monogram GR on postboxes

explanation.surface: The royal monogram of King George I is mentioned, along with someone close to death.
explanation.walkthrough: George I's royal cipher is G I R (Georgius Primus Rex); spell the I as a word. The definition plays on 'cipher' meaning a nobody: someone about to become one is close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, a person or thing doomed and past saving will shortly be dead or finished.

clue.text: The mark of a whip denoting wellbeing

definitions.meaning: a raised ridge on the skin left by a lash

explanation.surface: A lash scar is oddly said to signify good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a ridge raised on skin by a lash, and archaic prosperity or welfare.

clue.text: Let it stand in the toothpaste tube

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave something standing inside a tube of toothpaste.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the proofreader's Latin instruction meaning ignore the correction and keep the original.

clue.text: Where St Augustine made his mark as a beast

definitions.text: Where St Augustine made his mark
definitions.meaning: ... Regius in North Africa, where Augustine was bishop
short for the river horse of Africa

explanation.surface: A remark about where the famous saint did his work, wrongly calling him an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustine was Bishop of the North African city of that name; it is also the short form of a large African river mammal.

clue.text: Bag-every single one of the suspects

definitions.meaning: a large travel bag that takes everything

definitions.text: every single one of the suspects
definitions.meaning: an instruction to detain all of them

explanation.surface: Police are told to bag up and detain every suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A capacious travelling bag, and a command to detain everyone suspected.

clue.text: High distinction given to writer by America for collected writings

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a top British honour
a nib is the writing point of a pen
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An honour goes to an author from America for their anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: A single volume containing several works by one author or various authors.

clue.text: Ageing medico doing duty at the end of month

parts.note: growing old, so the adjective for advanced years
MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
ON as in 'on duty', working at one's post

explanation.surface: An elderly army doctor working shifts as the month draws to its close.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches 'end of month' to the lunar month's final phase.
explanation.definitionFit: The waning lunar phase comes at the close of the lunar cycle, the original sense of month.

clue.text: Cul-de-sac reached by confessing that one is no longer up to date

parts.note: said in the first person, 'one is' becomes I'm
passé is French-derived for old-fashioned, behind the times

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a dead end admits they've fallen behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confessing that' tells you to put the words in the speaker's mouth: I'm passé.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead end is a road with no way out, and figuratively a deadlock.

clue.text: Took a good look, I'd say

indicators.note: a cue that the word is spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: the contraction of 'I would', pronounced the same as the past tense of watching

explanation.surface: Someone casually remarks that they had a careful look, they suppose.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have looked at something carefully or watched it closely.

clue.text: Turn up the gas ring for the pudding

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
O is the shape of a ring

explanation.surface: A cook turns up the burner to make a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads like raising the flame, but it reverses GAS to SAG in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk pudding made from palm-starch granules is a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Sicilian tourists should see it-before returning

indicators.note: the word goes back the way it came, read in reverse

parts.note: ante is Latin for before

explanation.surface: Advice that visitors to Sicily should take in the sight before going home.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous active volcano on Sicily is a major sight for visitors.

clue.text: Docked antelope shows vigour

indicators.note: docking an animal cuts off its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A tailless antelope still displays great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flair, dash and energy.

clue.text: Fight with orange?

parts.note: a pun on the navel orange: a combat fought with that citrus fruit would sound like a clash of warships

explanation.surface: An absurd image of people pelting each other with oranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash between fleets at sea, punned on the navel orange, which sounds identical.

clue.text: Bad language indicates one's truthfulness

definitions.meaning: a solemn vow, as sworn in court

explanation.surface: Swearing is offered as proof that someone is honest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a profanity and a solemn sworn promise.

clue.text: Evidence of murder is not so bald as made out

indicators.note: the letters are worked out or reshaped into another form

explanation.surface: Someone claims a man is less bald than reported, beside a murder inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as made out' is the anagram signal: shuffle IS NOT SO BALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks of spilt gore at a crime scene are classic forensic signs of a killing.
